query: For a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy initially in a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-containing state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its subsequent microstructural evolution and the associated retention or loss of corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance? The hypothesis should address the unresolved transformation pathway and kinetics while accounting for the tendency of these alloys to develop intermetallic compounds. Specify an unnamed controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to the initial state, the relevant service-regime boundaries, supporting evidence from reported Mg-containing alloys, and a clear falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: In Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys (L-HEAs) that are quenched into a supersaturated single-phase solid solution, the first step of microstructural evolution during subsequent thermal exposure (250 – 650 °C) is a chemically driven spinodal-like decomposition that produces nano-scale Mg-rich and Mg-lean compositional waves.  At moderate temperatures (≤450 °C) the decomposition remains fine and Mg continues to diffuse toward and enrich the alloy surface, enabling rapid nucleation of a compact, adherent MgO-rich scale that preserves aqueous corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.  When the same alloy is exposed at higher temperatures (>550 °C) or for longer times, the Mg-rich regions coarsen and transform into equilibrium intermetallic compounds (e.g., C14 (Mg,Al)2Ca or Al12Mg17-type phases).  This consumes mobile Mg, interrupts Mg outward diffusion, and leaves a Mg-depleted matrix that supports formation of permeable Cr- or Al-rich oxides, thereby degrading corrosion/oxidation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, water-quenched Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy (e.g., Al15Mg20Li20Zn20Cu25 at.% class) exhibiting a single supersaturated BCC solid solution with <10 nm compositional fluctuation amplitude revealed by anomalous SAXS.
generation.intervention: Isothermal aging for 100 h in air at (i) 400 °C (moderate) versus (ii) 600 °C (elevated).
generation.conditions: Ambient atmosphere for corrosion testing; laboratory air for oxidation; no mechanical load; identical surface finish; sample thickness ≤2 mm.
generation.structural_mediator: Temperature-dependent evolution of Mg-rich compositional modulations that either remain as nano-scale spinodal waves or transform into coarse intermetallic precipitates.
generation.mechanism: Negative Mg-matrix mixing enthalpy drives uphill diffusion and continuous spinodal decomposition.  At higher temperature the amplified concentration waves exceed a critical wavelength, providing periodic nuclei for classical nucleation and growth of equilibrium Mg-containing intermetallics, which in turn drain Mg from the matrix and inhibit Mg surface segregation, altering oxide chemistry.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the initial quenched state:  • After 400 °C/100 h (Sample-A) – HRTEM/APT reveal 5–15 nm Mg-rich/lean modulations; XRD shows no new intermetallic peaks; surface XPS shows MgO-rich layer; electrochemical polarization curves and 800 °C TGA show corrosion/oxidation rates within ±20 % of the as-quenched baseline.  • After 600 °C/100 h (Sample-B) – XRD and TEM reveal ≥50 nm Mg- and Al-rich intermetallics; APT shows matrix Mg loss (>50 % reduction); surface oxide shifts to mixed (Al,Cr)2O3 with porosity; corrosion/oxidation rates increase by ≥3× over baseline.
generation.baseline: As-quenched solid-solution sample tested without prior aging, exhibiting low corrosion current density (≤1 µA cm⁻² in 0.6 M NaCl) and parabolic oxidation rate constant k_p ≤ 1×10⁻¹² kg² m⁻⁴ s⁻¹ at 800 °C.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis expected to hold for Mg-containing L-HEAs where overall Mg content is 10–25 at.% and initial state is a single supersaturated solid solution; outside this range (Mg <5 at.% or alloys already containing equilibrium intermetallics) the proposed pathway may not operate.
generation.uncertainty: Direct evidence of spinodal modulation in Mg-containing HEAs is limited; the critical wavelength and transition temperature to nucleation-controlled intermetallic formation remain to be quantified.  Surface segregation kinetics of Mg could be altered by trace impurities or prior cold work, potentially masking the predicted effects.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three identical coupons in the stated initial condition.  Age two coupons at 400 °C and 600 °C, respectively, for 100 h; keep one unaged.  Perform (i) in-situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction during aging to detect emergent intermetallic reflections, (ii) 3D atom-probe tomography and STEM-EDS to map Mg partitioning after aging, (iii) XPS/ToF-SIMS depth profiling of surface oxides, and (iv) potentiodynamic polarization in 0.6 M NaCl plus thermogravimetric oxidation at 800 °C/4 h.
measurements: In-situ XRD peak appearance for intermetallic phases
Spinodal wavelength and amplitude from SAXS/HRTEM
Mg atomic fraction in matrix from APT
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if any two of the following occur: (1) 600 °C aging does NOT produce new intermetallic peaks or coarse precipitates while Mg matrix concentration drops by <10 %; (2) 400 °C aging DOES produce the same intermetallics/coarsening as 600 °C; (3) Surface Mg enrichment and MgO-rich oxide are absent after 400 °C aging; (4) Corrosion and oxidation rates of 600 °C aged sample do NOT exceed those of the baseline by at least a factor of 2.
